subject: Sovereign boundary: APAC warm-standby options for EU customers
messages:
From: Anne Svensson <anne.svensson@skandia-bank.se>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 07:58:00 +02:00
Subject: Sovereign boundary: APAC warm-standby options for EU customers

Hi Rishi,

Quick question from our cloud compliance team — we have an EU production deployment for one of our retail banking lines and the regulators are asking us to design for continuity if the EU region becomes unavailable. We're considering an APAC warm-standby for compute (no hot DR, just warm standby for throughput) but residency of personal data must remain in the EU unless explicitly allowed.

Can Redwood support a model where:
- Production (primary model weights, audit logs, and billing metadata) stays in the EU;
- APAC warm-standby can accept traffic during failover but only after a gated transfer/approval;
- Replication to APAC is either limited to encrypted blobs (no cleartext PII) or uses tokenized payloads with EU-held keys;
- Audit logs are still queryable by our compliance team without leaving the EU in cleartext.

We also need to understand the networking implications — BGP/peering, DNS TTLs, and whether any persistent connections (KV caches, pre-warmed sessions) will force data out of the EU. Finally, any constraints re: customer-managed KMS / HSM are important.

Can you send a short design note and a practical runbook we can review with compliance next week?

Thanks,
Anne Svensson
Head of Cloud Ops
Skandia Bank

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Anne Svensson <anne.svensson@skandia-bank.se>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 11:03:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Sovereign boundary: APAC warm-standby options for EU customers

Anne — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Soojin (inference infra) and Marcus (solutions) to sketch a practical option set. I attached a working "failover matrix" that maps tradeoffs and a short questionnaire for compliance.

High level options we can support (short):
1) EU-active / APAC-warm (tokenized replication): weights and PII remain in EU. APAC receives tokenized payloads and a minimal model shard for inference. Keys remain in EU HSM. Replay/failover occurs only after explicit customer approval (manual or via an agreed automation).
2) EU-active / APAC-warm (encrypted-blob replication): encrypted artifacts replicate to APAC. Keys remain in EU; decryption only possible with customer-managed KMS which we do not export.
3) Full EU-only standby: no replication of data out of EU. APAC hosts pre-built model artifacts (no customer data), longer RTO.

Networking notes (short):
- BGP / peering + DNS: prefer low TTL and app-level health checks. We recommend an active path with weighted DNS + regional egress policies.
- Persistent KV caches: these will live in-region; cross-region cache warm-up is possible only with tokenized/hashed keys.
- Connections: session metadata may be proxied; avoid sending PII in connection-level metadata.

Attached: eu-apac-failover-matrix.xlsx (working draft, rows=options/tradeoffs/ops steps) and draft-residency-questions.pdf (compliance questions). Also dropping HubSpot deal for context: https://hubspot.com/deal/HD-45812

Soojin / Marcus — can you add the deployment-level constraints (firewall rules, peering play, KMS flow) and a minimal runbook? Meeting with Anne + compliance scheduled for Thu if possible.

—Rishi
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: eu-apac-failover-matrix.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 42KB), draft-residency-questions.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Anne Svensson <anne.svensson@skandia-bank.se>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 18:35:00 +09:00
Subject: Re: Sovereign boundary: APAC warm-standby options for EU customers

Anne / Rishi — technical reply and constraints below. I'll keep this pragmatic so compliance has something concrete to review.

Proposed architecture (EU-active, APAC warm-standby, customer-managed keys):
- Control plane: customer-managed control plane (Private deployment) hosted in EU VPC. Control plane metadata, audit logs, model version entitlements remain stored in EU storage (encrypted).
- Data plane (inference): EU inference cluster serves normal traffic. An APAC standby cluster exists with only model binaries and cached tokenizer shards — no decrypted customer payloads at rest by default.
- Replication: snapshot-based replication of non-PII model metadata and encrypted KV snapshot to APAC. Encrypted blobs use the customer's KMS (CMK) resident in EU. APAC stores ciphertext only. Decryption requires the CMK which we keep reachable only from EU control plane unless customer approves temporary key grant (KMS key policy + IAM).
- Failover gating: automated health checks OR manual approval. Automated path should only flip traffic to APAC for non-PII endpoints or where the customer has enabled key escrow/temporary key grants. Otherwise manual process (runbook step) is required.

Networking specifics:
- Peering & routing: Establish VPC peering between customer EU VPC and Redwood's EU Private nodes. APAC standby peered similarly in APAC. Use BGP with route-priority and health-probes on the NAT/gateway.
- DNS strategy: low TTL (30s) and weighted DNS with health-check failover. Combine with regional ingress policies in the app-tier to avoid sticky global routes.
- Egress & firewall: Block outbound connections from APAC standby cluster to customer-controlled KMS endpoints unless explicit allowlist is provided. APAC should have a deny-by-default firewall; only allow specific ephemeral connections to EU KMS when customer enables key grant.
- KV cache warm-up: use hashed keys and tokenization. Do not replicate raw user text. Cache seeding can use pre-warmed prompts (synthetic) and model slices.

Operational constraints / compliance:
- Audit logs: keep primary logs in EU. For operational troubleshooting, we can ship redacted logs to APAC (hashes + metadata) but not PII. Full logs remain queryable in EU via a secure audit interface (read-only for regulator accounts).
- KMS & HSM: recommend customer-managed CMK with key policy restricting decryption to EU principals; Redwood will request temporary grants via IAM only under explicit customer approval.
- RPO/RTO realism: warm standby expected RTO 30-90 mins (depends on how much state you permit to pre-warm). Full EU-only standby RTO will be higher but guarantees zero cross-border data flow.

Runbook pointers (short):
- Detect incident -> evaluate region health -> check KMS key-policy -> if key grant present, start staged traffic shift to APAC (weighted DNS 80/20 -> 50/50 -> 100/0) -> monitor artifacts and audit logs -> confirm with compliance -> finalize.

Known limitations:
- Latency-sensitive customers will notice increased p99 after switch; consider degraded SLA or emergency quota bump.
- Legal teams sometimes disallow any cross-border replication of metadata with identifiers — in that case we default to EU-only standby.

I'll draft a one-page runbook and a checklist for compliance before the Thu meeting. Marcus, can you add the customer ops contacts and an action list for the call?

—Soojin
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anne Svensson <anne.svensson@skandia-bank.se>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:15:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Sovereign boundary: APAC warm-standby options for EU customers

Anne — thanks for the prompt. Quick summary and next steps from our side: 

Decisions / recommended path:
- Default recommendation: EU-active with APAC warm-standby using encrypted-blob replication + customer-managed CMK (Option 2). This balances continuity and residency.
- Failover gating: require explicit approval from Skandia (automated can be enabled later with documented key grants).
- Audit logs: primary in EU; redacted metadata can be replicated for ops but not PII.

Action items before Thu compliance call: 
1) Redwood: produce a 1-page runbook and a 2-page technical appendix (network diagrams + KMS flow). (Owner: Soojin)
2) Redwood: convert the failover-matrix into a compliance checklist (Owner: Rishi)
3) Skandia: confirm whether temporary KMS grants are acceptable and provide the external ops contact for Tokyo (we'll loop Takashi if needed).
4) Redwood & Skandia: schedule a short tech-level PoC window (2 weeks) — target start 2027-05-24.

I'll upload the runbook draft and the tech appendix to our drive and send an invite for Thu. Links: https://drive.redwood.com/open?id=1a2b3c-residency-draft

If you confirm KMS approach and give us a PoC window, engineering can prepare a minimal PoC that proves failover gating without replicating decrypted logs.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
